name: Kensington and Chelsea

council.name: Royal Borough of Kensington and Chelsea

licensing.selective: No selective licensing scheme is in force; homes let to a single household do not need a council licence.
licensing.additional: A borough-wide additional HMO licensing scheme came into force on 1 June 2023 and expires on 31 May 2028. It covers most HMOs let to three or more people from two or more households sharing a kitchen, bathroom or toilet that fall outside mandatory licensing.
licensing.fee: About £1,493 for an additional HMO licence (Part A £1,004 on application, Part B £489 once approved, plus £72 for each extra room), with a £200 discount for accredited landlords (council HMO licensing FAQs).

rent.text: £3,739 a month (ONS, September 2026), up 3.0% on a year earlier; the highest average rent of any local authority in the UK

price.text: £1,204,000 (UK HPI, August 2026, provisional), down 13.8% on a year earlier

privateRentedShare.text: 39.6% of households rent privately (Census 2021), up from 35.8% in 2011

councilTax.text: £1,643.44 (Band D, 2026/27, including the GLA precept); a little more in the garden square areas, which pay an extra levy

housing: Kensington and Chelsea is the most expensive place to rent in the country, and about four in ten households rent privately. Most homes are flats: lateral and duplex flats in stucco terraces, red-brick mansion blocks and mews houses, many with porters, lifts and shared garden squares. North Kensington is different, with large post-war estates and towers, and the borough saw England's biggest rise in social renting between 2011 and 2021. Short and corporate lets and high-value furnished tenancies are common, so inventories tend to list a lot of contents.
checkinTips: Furnished high-value lets: photograph each piece of furniture, rugs, curtains and artwork close up, and record makes of appliances.
Mansion blocks with porters: note fobs, porter-held keys, post box keys and lift access, and photograph the communal entrance.
Stucco terraces: photograph the front steps, railings, balconies and any cracked or flaking stucco visible from the flat.
Mews houses: photograph the garage door, its remote and any cobbled forecourt, and check for damp in ground-floor rooms.
Garden square access: record the garden key or card and any terms that come with it.
Basement and lower-ground flats: photograph lightwells, vault storage under the pavement, and walls at floor level for damp.
tenantHelp: The council's environmental health team (private sector housing) can inspect privately rented homes for disrepair and hazards and enforces HMO licensing; contact it through the housing pages of rbkc.gov.uk.
